items.title: Houthi Threat to Red Sea Shipping Rises
items.summary: Houthi militants are ramping up attacks along Yemen’s Red Sea coast, shutting operations at a strategic seaport and pushing closer to the Bab al-Mandeb, a critical shipping chokepoint, The Wall Street Journal’s Jared Malsin and Saleh al-Batati write.  The militant group’s recent missile and drone attacks forced the closure of the port of Mokha, a key logistics hub for civilian shipping and for anti-Houthi forces operating along the coast, Yemeni authorities said.  Shutting down the port makes it harder for the anti-Houthi forces to resupply and resist Houthi attacks.

items.title: China's Pony.ai plans to deploy more than 4,000 robotaxis abroad
items.summary: Chinese autonomous driving company Pony.ai has a pipeline of planned and potential overseas robotaxi deployments of more than 4,000 vehicles, ‌it said on Tuesday, as it seeks to accelerate its expansion beyond ‌China.  Autonomous driving firms are racing to commercialise robotaxi services overseas.  As the technology matures and domestic competition intensifies, ​they are seeking new revenue streams and partnerships in markets including the Middle East, Asia and Europe.

items.title: Jim Cramer Has This ‘Great Long-Term’ Ride-Hailing Stock on His Radar: ‘I Am a Buyer’
items.summary: TV Host Jim Cramer has backed ride-hailing giant Uber Technologies Inc. (NYSE:UBER) on Monday, calling it a good long-term stock. Jim Cramer Says Buy Uber on Lightning Round On CNBC’s “Mad Money Lightning Round” show, Cramer shared bullish sentiments on Uber, saying that it was “one great long-term stock” and that he would not be “backing away” from the company’s stock. “The answer is, I am a buyer of Uber,” Cramer said on the show.
